title: He made Himself
hook: He created Himself, then the Name, then the world, and sat watching it with delight (Asa di Var 1, ang 463)

segments.voice: Yesterday, chaanan: a hundred moons can't light the inside; the guru is the light. Today, the first pauri, the first rung of the ballad.

A potter finishes a bowl, sets it on the shelf, and steps back. A gardener stands at the edge of a bed she planted in spring, now full of tomatoes. A father watches his daughter take her first wobbly steps across the kitchen. There's a look on a maker's face in that moment, half pride and half wonder, as if they can't quite believe it's real. The first pauri of Asa di Var says God has that look too.
screen: `A POTTER STEPS BACK.` → `A GARDEN FULL OF TOMATOES.` → `THE LOOK ON A MAKER'S FACE.`

segments.voice: The first pauri begins, in paraphrase: He Himself fashioned Himself, and Himself took on the Name. Second, He made the creation, and seated within it, He watches it with delight. Then it turns to praise: You are the Giver and the Maker; pleased, You give and bless. You know everyone; You give life and can take it back with a word. Take the order slowly. First, aapeenai aap saajio: He made Himself. Nobody made God. God is self-existent, the same idea Sikhs recite every day in the Mool Mantar as saibhang. Second, the Name: God takes on naau, which in Gurbani means God made known, God expressed. Only then the world, kudrat, the creation. Then the lovely part: kar aasan, having taken a seat, ditho chaau, He watched with delight. Aasan is a seat, the cushion or mat you sit on. God doesn't make the world and leave, like a builder handing over keys. God sits down inside it. And chaau is delight, eagerness, the joy of a festival or a wedding. So the God of this first pauri isn't a distant engineer or a grim judge. It's a maker who sits down in the middle of the work and enjoys it. That says something about the world, too. If its Maker watches it with delight, it's worth delighting in: tomatoes, first steps, the bowl on the shelf. Before Asa di Var gets sharp about pride and pretending, as it will, it sets this down first: a world made with joy.
screen: `FIRST: HE MADE HIMSELF.` · `THEN THE NAME, THEN THE WORLD.` · `AASAN: HE SITS DOWN INSIDE IT.` · `CHAAU: DELIGHT, LIKE A FESTIVAL.` · then, large: `WATCHING WITH DELIGHT.`

segments.voice: Picture something you made, a meal, a garden, a letter, a friendship you tended, and sit with it the way the pauri says God sits with creation. Not judging the flaws; just watching, with delight. If you pray, rest in Waheguru, the Maker who watches with delight.
Chaau, delight or eagerness: Asa di Var's first pauri says God made Himself, then the Name, then the world, and took a seat within it, watching with chaau.
Your line: watching with delight. The Maker never left the workshop. Day five hundred forty, done.

howItsDone: The first pauri of Asa di Var, sung each morning in gurdwaras, describes God as self-made, taking on the Name, making the world, and sitting within it to watch with delight.
